author: yellowstone times
title: Montana State University Extension honors staff members at annual conference
text:
Montana State University Extension recently honored its staff, faculty, and partners at the annual MSU Extension conference in Bozeman. The awards recognized individuals and groups for their contributions to communities across Montana.
“We are fortunate to have accomplished faculty and staff making a positive impact on the people and places of Montana,” said Cody Stone, executive director of MSU Extension. “It is an honor to recognize their contributions through our awards program.”
The Director’s Office annually recognizes outstanding faculty and staff who achieve success in their fields or provide exceptional service to their communities. Adam Sigler received the Innovative Engagement Award for his ongoing work with Montanans on water issues. Shelley Mills and Patrick Mangan were given the Team Award for co-chairing a national meeting that hosted over 1,200 participants. Other honorees included Allison Kosto with the Distinguished Faculty Award, Abiya Saeed with the Early Career Faculty Award, and Jason Killam with the Distinguished Staff Award.
Montana’s Joint Council of Extension Professionals also presented several honors. Dan Clark was awarded the 2025 Silver Buffalo Award for two decades of service as director of the MSU Extension Local Government Center. Janell Barber received recognition for her achievements in programs involving people development, while the Arrowhead Award went to a coalition focused on youth mental health that includes school counselors from Ronan, St. Ignatius, Arlee schools, and community health educators from the Confederated Salish and Kootenai Tribes. Julie Gagnon was recognized for her leadership as an administrative assistant.
The Montana chapter of Epsilon Sigma Phi presented additional awards to individuals such as Kaleena Miller (Early Career), Lisa Terry (Mid-Career), Jason Killam (Meritorious Support), Katie Weaver (Visionary Leadership), Jane Wolery (Administrative Leadership), Brenda Richey (Outreach and Engagement), Peter Kolb (Distinguished Service), Shelley Mills and Inga Hawbaker as part of Rooted in Montana (Distinguished Team), and Sabra Brooks, Tammy Young, Jennifer Cheff with the 4-H Mentoring Program (Friend of Extension).
Molly Yurdana and Makayla Paul received Achievement in Service awards from the Montana Association of Extension 4-H Agents; Ben Hauptman and Kellie Kahtani were honored for Youth Development Distinguished Service; Allison Kosto earned a Meritorious Service Award; Sharla Sackman was recognized for 25 years of service.
Jeanette Allday was acknowledged by the Montana Extension Association of Family and Consumer Sciences for innovative nutrition programming. The Family Health and Wellness Award went to Brenda Richey, Havilah Burton, and Tammy Sandberg for addressing food insecurity on the Flathead Indian Reservation. Lisa Terry won national recognition for her outreach work supporting rural communities’ needs regarding food security, safety, and youth mental health.
Kari Lewis received an Achievement in Service award from the Montana Association of County Agricultural Agents while Marc King earned a Distinguished Service award.
